messages.subject: data across all tabPanel
parts:
I am trying to build a shiny app to display estimates of various estimated demographic indicators by age, sex and education. I have a basic example on our server....
http://witt.null2.net/shiny/temp/
the ui.R, server.R and do_data.R (where I generate and save the data) files are available here:
https://github.com/gjabel/temp

Everything is a bit clunky though, especially when I play the animaition. I think some these problems might be due to the data size (+3million lines), which I can live with....using the saves package i manage to load the data pretty quickly. I suspect though that I could speed things up using some better R coding. For each tabPanel I am having to load the indicator data through my getdf1(), even if there are no changes in input$indicator. Is there a better alternative, where I can create df1 for all tabs, and update if and when the user changes in the indicator? I was playing around with observe and isolate function, but I could not get anything to work (I am not sure I fully understand them yet).

Cheers.

messages.author: 129e07bdb789652f
messages.subject: Re: data across all tabPanel
parts: For each tabPanel I am having to load the indicator data through my getdf1(), even if there are no changes in input$indicator.

I don't think so : 

  getdf1<- reactive({
    df1<-NULL
    if(!is.null(input$indicator)){
      df1<-loads(file="df1", variables=input$indicator, ultra.fast = TRUE, to.data.frame=TRUE)
      df1<-cbind(df0,df1)
    }
    return(df1)
  })

Here getdf1() is a reactive conductor. It does not work like a function: when your app finds getdf1() in server.R, that does not execute the body of getdf1().: that only get the output of getdf1(), and this one is not updated while input$indicator does not change.
